---
title: "Tool 2 — Gaussian Monte-Carlo"
subtitle: "Right correlation, thin tails; the VaR gap"
---



*Learn-the-tool track · Lab 2 of 3.*

Gaussian Monte-Carlo matches the covariance — and still understates joint risk,
because Gaussian tails are thin and tail-independent.  You will measure the VaR
gap it leaves.

---

## 1 · A Tail-Dependent Pair, and Its Gaussian Twin

::: {#b4a075d1 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
n = 4000
z = rng.normal(0, 1, n)
a = 0.5 * z + 0.5 * rng.normal(0, 1, n)
b = 0.5 * z + 0.5 * rng.normal(0, 1, n)
crash = rng.random(n) < 0.05
shock = np.abs(rng.standard_t(2.5, n) * 3.0)
a, b = np.where(crash, a - shock, a), np.where(crash, b - shock, b)
D = np.column_stack([a, b]); D = (D - D.mean(0)) / D.std(0)

gmc = rng.multivariate_normal(D.mean(0), np.cov(D.T), size=n)

print(f"covariance matched? real corr {np.corrcoef(D.T)[0,1]:.2f} "
      f"vs GMC {np.corrcoef(gmc.T)[0,1]:.2f}")
print(f"co-crash:  real {cocrash_fraction(D[:,0], D[:,1], 0.02):.0%}  "
      f"vs GMC {cocrash_fraction(gmc[:,0], gmc[:,1], 0.02):.0%}  (deep tail)")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
covariance matched? real corr 0.87 vs GMC 0.88
co-crash:  real 91%  vs GMC 52%  (deep tail)
```
:::
:::


The two clouds share a middle but not a tail — see where they part:

::: {#cell-fig-tool2-clouds .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, data, col, name in [
    (axL, D, COOL, f"real · co-crash {cocrash_fraction(D[:,0], D[:,1], 0.02):.0%}"),
    (axR, gmc, CRASH, f"Gaussian MC · co-crash {cocrash_fraction(gmc[:,0], gmc[:,1], 0.02):.0%}"),
]:
    ax.scatter(data[:, 0], data[:, 1], s=6, c=col, alpha=0.3, edgecolors="none")
    ax.axvspan(-10, np.quantile(D[:, 0], 0.02), color=INK, alpha=0.05)
    ax.axhspan(-10, np.quantile(D[:, 1], 0.02), color=INK, alpha=0.05)
    ax.set_title(name, fontsize=11); ax.set_xlim(-8, 4); ax.set_ylim(-8, 4)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}

## 2 · The VaR Gap

::: {#84e61f09 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
port_real, port_gmc = D[:, 0] + D[:, 1], gmc[:, 0] + gmc[:, 1]
for ql in [0.05, 0.01, 0.005]:
    vr, vg = np.quantile(port_real, ql), np.quantile(port_gmc, ql)
    print(f"{ql:>6.1%} VaR:  real {vr:+.2f}   GMC {vg:+.2f}   "
          f"understated by {vr - vg:+.2f}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
  5.0% VaR:  real -1.58   GMC -3.15   understated by +1.57
  1.0% VaR:  real -7.26   GMC -4.44   understated by -2.82
  0.5% VaR:  real -11.28   GMC -4.97   understated by -6.31
```
:::
:::


::: {#cell-fig-tool2-gmc .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
bins = np.linspace(min(port_real.min(), port_gmc.min()), 3, 60)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.4))
ax.hist(port_real, bins=bins, density=True, color=COOL, alpha=0.55, label="real")
ax.hist(port_gmc, bins=bins, density=True, color=CRASH, alpha=0.45, label="Gaussian MC")
ax.axvline(np.quantile(port_real, 0.01), color=COOL, lw=2, ls="--")
ax.axvline(np.quantile(port_gmc, 0.01), color=CRASH, lw=2, ls="--")
ax.set_xlabel("portfolio return"); ax.set_ylabel("density")
ax.set_title("1% VaR: real vs Gaussian MC", fontsize=12)
ax.legend(fontsize=9, frameon=False); despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Portfolio loss distribution: the Gaussian MC misses the deep-loss tail and reports a too-optimistic 1% VaR.](lab-tool2-gaussian-mc_files/figure-html/fig-tool2-gmc-output-1.png){#fig-tool2-gmc width=884 height=513}
:::
:::


::: {.callout-tip}
## What to Look for
The deeper the quantile, the wider the gap — Gaussian tail-independence means the
error *grows* exactly where it hurts.  Matching covariance is not matching tail
risk.
:::
